column1: # terms.tsv (harbor#950) — THE ONLY PLACE the controlled vocabulary exists.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. A name is a tuple of vocabulary terms rendered once per surface
# (standards/naming.md §0). Before this file the vocabulary lived in prose, in the lint's
# regexes and in each reader's head, so a word could mean two things and nothing noticed.
# bin/lint-name.sh reads this file and nothing else for the term sets, and the glossary,
# naming guide, CLI tree, label set and Vale config are generated from it. Change a term
# here and the lint result and the generated glossary change with no other edit.
# SEED. The concept rows come from research/02 §1 (219 concepts, harbor#949), with the
# standard's own classes laid over them: families and verbs (§3), kinds (§4), layers (§5),
# domains, clients and abbreviations (D-18, D-26, D-35), plus two classes the lint needs:
# `system` (a repo name usable as an env prefix, D-15) and `extension` (§6.3's registered
# extension chain), and `subject` (the lint subject families of §3). Every closed set is a
# class here, never prose or code (09a S4): mode, outcome, decision, severity, state (D-29),
# control-type, moment, function, lifecycle (D-62), and level (D-57).
# COLUMNS  id <TAB> class <TAB> pref <TAB> broader <TAB> vsm <TAB> stability <TAB> successor
#   id          the canonical word: lowercase kebab, a digit never starts a word
#   class       one or more of family verb domain client abbreviation kind layer concept
#               system extension subject level mode outcome decision severity priority state
#               control-type moment function lifecycle share relation modality tier commit-type, comma-separated.
#               family and verb never overlap. level terms form one containment chain by `broader` (D-57).
#               relation: the typed edges a policy row or a kind's required_relations names (research/15 §3).
#               modality: duty, prohibition, permission (ODRL). tier: constitutional, policy, standard, repo,
#               control, highest first; a tier term that shares its id with a family or concept carries the class too.
#   pref        the preferred term in prose
#   broader     the parent term's id, or -; gives the hierarchy (lint -> audit -> control-plane)
#   vsm         viable-system function, shown in the glossary and never in a name (D-27)
#   stability   experimental | stable | deprecated; a deprecated row names its successor (D-19)
#   alt         discovery labels from the seed, `; `-separated. NOT enforced: the aliases the
#               lint rejects or confines are rows in aliases.tsv. On a mode term the labels are
#               the legacy spellings of that mode a controls.tsv cell may still use and the lint
#               reads as it (D-64: advisory and inform are read as warn, never written).
#   depends_on  the families this family may use through their public entry, comma-separated,
#               or - (M3, D-60). On a severity: the one priority term (p0..p3) it sets by default (harbor#1001). It is the allowed edge list the reference graph (harbor#996)
#               will check; the lint refuses a name that is not a family and any cycle.
